title: Ideal Gas — 40 MCQs
description: Pressure and volume coefficients of a gas, Charles's and Boyle's laws, absolute zero, the ideal gas equation, molecules and Avogadro's number, assumptions of the kinetic-molecular model, pressure of a gas, root mean square speed, and the relation between pressure, kinetic energy and temperature.

questions.q: The law which states that at constant temperature the product of the pressure and the volume of a given mass of gas is constant is
questions.explanation: Boyle's law gives PV = constant at constant temperature; Charles's law relates volume and temperature at constant pressure.

questions.q: Charles's law for a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure states that
questions.explanation: At constant pressure the volume of a given mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature, V/T = constant.

questions.q: The absolute zero of temperature on the Celsius scale is
questions.explanation: Absolute zero is 0 K, which corresponds to −273.15 °C on the Celsius scale; all gases would theoretically have zero volume there at constant pressure.

questions.q: The equation of state of an ideal gas for n moles is
questions.explanation: Combining Boyle's law (PV = constant) and Charles's law (V ∝ T) for n moles gives the ideal gas equation PV = nRT.

questions.q: Avogadro's number is
questions.explanation: One mole of any substance contains 6.022 × 10²³ molecules (or particles); this number is Avogadro's number.

questions.q: The SI unit of the universal gas constant R is
questions.explanation: From PV = nRT, R = PV/(nT), so its unit is (N m²)(m)/(mol K) = J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.q: For a fixed mass of gas kept at constant pressure, the volume at absolute zero temperature would theoretically become
questions.explanation: Since V ∝ T at constant pressure, the V–T graph is a straight line which, when produced backwards, meets the temperature axis at T = 0 K, where V = 0.

questions.q: The average translational kinetic energy of one molecule of an ideal gas is
questions.explanation: From kinetic theory the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas is (3/2)kT, where k is Boltzmann's constant.

questions.q: The root mean square speed of the molecules of a gas of molar mass M at absolute temperature T is
questions.explanation: Equating (1/3)ρc̄² with the gas pressure gives the root mean square speed as √(3RT/M) for one mole of an ideal gas.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of the kinetic-molecular model of an ideal gas?
options: A gas consists of a very large number of molecules
The volume of the molecules is negligible compared with the volume of the container
The molecules attract one another with strong intermolecular forces
questions.explanation: In an ideal gas the intermolecular forces are assumed to be negligible; strong attraction between molecules belongs to real gases, not to the ideal-gas model.

questions.q: The root mean square speed of oxygen molecules at 300 K is about (M = 32 g mol⁻¹, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
The average translational kinetic energy of one mole of an ideal gas at 300 K is (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
At the same temperature, the ratio of the root mean square speed of hydrogen molecules (M = 2 g mol⁻¹) to that of oxygen molecules (M = 32 g mol⁻¹) is
questions.explanation: At the same temperature c_rms ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(32/2) = √16 = 4, i.e. 4 : 1.

questions.q: The number of molecules in 1 cm³ of an ideal gas at STP (1.01 × 10⁵ Pa, 273 K) is about
A gas occupies 200 cm³ at 27 °C. Keeping the pressure constant, its volume at 127 °C will be
questions.explanation: V/T = constant, so V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 200 × 400/300 = 266.7 cm³.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas is at 0 °C at a pressure of 1 atm. Keeping the volume constant, the gas is heated to 273 °C. Its new pressure is
questions.explanation: At constant volume P ∝ T, so P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 1 × (273 + 273)/(0 + 273) = 546/273 = 2 atm.

questions.q: The pressure of a gas is 1 × 10⁵ Pa and its density is 1.2 kg m⁻³. The root mean square speed of its molecules is
At what temperature will oxygen molecules (M = 32 g mol⁻¹) have the same root mean square speed as helium molecules (M = 4 g mol⁻¹) at 300 K?
The number of molecules in 3.2 g of oxygen gas (M = 32 g mol⁻¹) is
questions.explanation: Number of moles = 3.2/32 = 0.1, so the number of molecules = 0.1 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 6.022 × 10²².

questions.q: The volume occupied by 2 moles of an ideal gas at 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K is (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
The kinetic energy per unit volume of an ideal gas at a pressure of 1 × 10⁵ Pa is
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas, KE per unit volume = (3/2)P = 1.5 × 1 × 10⁵ = 1.5 × 10⁵ J m⁻³.

questions.q: For an ideal gas, the pressure coefficient and the volume coefficient are
questions.explanation: By Charles's law the volume coefficient is 1/273.15 per °C and by the pressure law the pressure coefficient is also 1/273.15 per °C; both follow from the same extrapolation of the gas laws to absolute zero.

questions.q: A gas at 2 atm occupies 600 cm³. It is compressed isothermally to 300 cm³. Its new pressure is
questions.explanation: For an isothermal change P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so P₂ = (2 × 600)/300 = 4 atm.

questions.q: The density of nitrogen (M = 28 g mol⁻¹) at 1 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K is about (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
The pressure of an ideal gas is doubled, its volume and mass remaining the same. The root mean square speed of its molecules becomes
questions.explanation: At constant volume and mass, P = (1/3)ρc̄² gives P ∝ c̄², so doubling P makes c_rms √2 times its original value.

questions.q: The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas at 373 K is (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹)
The total translational kinetic energy of 2 moles of an ideal gas at 300 K is (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

A gas occupies 500 cm³ at 27 °C and 1 atm. Its volume at 127 °C and 2 atm is
questions.explanation: From P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂, V₂ = P₁V₁T₂/(T₁P₂) = (1 × 500 × 400)/(300 × 2) = 333.3 cm³.

questions.q: A gas exerts a pressure of 1 atm at 0 °C. If it is heated at constant volume to 100 °C, its pressure becomes about
questions.explanation: At constant volume P ∝ T, so P₂ = 1 × (373.15/273.15) = 1.366 atm.

questions.q: When the temperature of a gas is raised from 27 °C to 327 °C, the percentage increase in the root mean square speed of its molecules is about
questions.explanation: T rises from 300 K to 600 K, so c_rms increases by the factor √2 = 1.414, an increase of (1.414 − 1) × 100 ≈ 41.4%.

The root mean square speed of the molecules of a gas at 300 K is 500 m s⁻¹. The temperature at which their root mean square speed becomes 1000 m s⁻¹ is
questions.explanation: Since c_rms ∝ √T, quadrupling c̄² means quadrupling T: T = 300 × (1000/500)² = 300 × 4 = 1200 K.

questions.q: The number of molecules per unit volume of an ideal gas at 1 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K is about (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹)
The average kinetic energy of a molecule of a gas at 27 °C is E. If the temperature is raised by 1 K, the percentage increase in E is about
questions.explanation: KE ∝ T, and T = 300 K, so the fractional increase is 1/300 = 0.0033, i.e. about 0.33%.

questions.q: The root mean square speed of hydrogen molecules (M = 2 g mol⁻¹) at 300 K is about (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
The pressure P exerted by an ideal gas is related to the translational kinetic energy E per unit volume of the gas by
questions.explanation: Since P = (1/3)ρc̄² and E = (1/2)ρc̄², we get P = (2/3)E, i.e. the pressure of a gas is two-thirds of its kinetic energy per unit volume.
